senses.def: (derivative of ἀγγέλλω ‘to tell, to inform,’ 33.189) the content of what has been announced
a person in the genealogy of Jesus

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to an extremely short period of time between a previous state or event and a subsequent state or event
senses.comment: In a number of contexts there is the implication of unexpectedness; but this seems to be a derivative of the context as a whole and not a part of the meaning of the lexical items.

senses.def: pertaining to being real and not imaginary
senses.comment: In some languages ‘the only one who is really God’ can only be expressed as ‘the only God who exists’ or ‘who is God and there are no other gods.’

senses.def: pertaining to being in accordance with historical fact
pertaining to being what something should be
one who takes care of a vineyard
to try to learn the nature or truth of something by the process of careful study, evaluation and judgment
to conduct a judicial inquiry
senses.comment: The use of ἀνακρίνω in 1 Corinthians 9:3 does not imply necessarily the strictly legal procedures of a courtroom. It is also possible to interpret ἀνακρίνω in 1 Corinthians 9:3 as meaning ‘to criticize’ or ‘to judge’ (see 33.412).

senses.def: to express disapproval of what someone has done
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἀνακρίνω in 1 Corinthians 9:3, see 56.12.

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: to make a judgment on the basis of careful and detailed information
pertaining to what will not go out of existence
to invite someone in return
unwillingness or refusal to comply with the demands of some authority
to refuse to believe the Christian message
glosses: to refuse to be a believer

senses.def: to respond to a question asking for information
to introduce or continue a somewhat formal discourse (occurring regularly with λέγω[a] ‘to say,’ 33.69)
senses.comment: A literal translation such as ‘at that time Jesus spoke and said’ (Matthew 11:25) may sound redundant in many languages.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being blameless in view of not having given offense
senses.comment: In a number of languages the concept of ‘being blameless’ as in 88.317 and 88.318 can only be expressed by a verbal expression involving some measure of complaint. For example, the expression in Acts 24:16 may be rendered as ‘I do my best to live in such a way that neither God nor people can blame me’ or ‘… can complain against me.’

senses.def: pertaining to not causing offense
pertaining to being qualified to perform some function
pertaining to not being bound or not regarding oneself as bound by any covenant or agreement
senses.comment: It is also possible to translate ἀσύνθετος in Romans 1:31 as ‘they feel no obligation to keep their agreements’ or ‘they do not feel bound to do what they have promised to do.’

senses.subdomain: Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
senses.def: pertaining to not loving what is good
glosses: being an enemy to what is good

senses.def: severe pain associated with torture and torment
senses.comment: A strictly literal translation of ὁ καπνὸς τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῶν may be seriously misleading, for it might imply that it is the smoke which causes the suffering, but it is clearly the fire which torments them (as indicated in Revelation 14:10). Therefore, ir may be necessary to translate ‘and the smoke of the fire that torments them.’

senses.def: pertaining to that which causes harm
senses.comment: There is no indication in 1 Timothy 6:9 as to the specific nature of the harm, but the extent of it is made clear in the following clause which speaks of complete destruction. This could be physical, moral, and/or spiritual.

senses.def: a number of possessions and valuables constituting an important and official asset of a political entity

senses.subdomain: To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
senses.def: that which is purposed or intended, with the implication of judgment or resolve

senses.subdomain: Have an Opinion, Hold a View
senses.def: that which is regarded or considered to be the case
senses.comment: It is also possible to under stand γνώμη in Philemon 1:14 as ‘agreement’ or ‘consent’ (see 31.14).

senses.def: agreement based on knowledge
senses.comment: This interpretation of γνώμη in Philemon 1:14 is less likely than the meaning of γνώμη as ‘opinion’ (see 31.3).

senses.def: to be fearful and cowardly
to make a judgment on legal matters, with the implication of thorough examination
glosses: to arrive at a verdict after examination

senses.def: (derivative of διατάσσω[a] ‘to order, to instruct,’ 33.325) that which has been specifically ordered or commanded
to break through a wall or barrier, normally by the process of digging through (usually implying a wall made of sun-dried brick)
an infectious disease of the intestinal tract, usually involving severe pain and diarrhea
senses.comment: In some languages one may speak of dysentery as ‘a watery discharge’ or ‘pain and discharge.’

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1:9)
to give justice to someone who has been wronged
to repay harm with harm, on the assumption that the initial harm was unjustified and that retribution is therefore called for
to punish, on the basis of what is rightly deserved
(derivative of ἐκτείνω ‘to stretch out,’ 16.19) pertaining to an unceasing activity, normally involving a degree of intensity and/or perseverance
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἐκτενής in 1 Peter 4:8, see ἐκτενής[b] 25.71.

senses.subdomain: Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
senses.def: pertaining to being eager to persevere in some state or activity
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἐκτενής in 1 Peter 4:8, see ἐκτενής[a] 68.12.

senses.def: to look forward with confidence to that which is good and beneficial
(derivative of ἐλπίζω[a] ‘to hope,’ 25.59) that which is hoped for
(derivative of ἐλπίζω[a] ‘to hope,’ 25.59) that which constitutes the cause or reason for hoping
senses.comment: This expression in 1 Thessalonians 2:19 may be rendered in some languages as ‘for who is the one who causes us to hope and to have joy’ or ‘… to be happy.’

senses.def: putting on and wearing clothes

senses.subdomain: Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
senses.def: to exclude or remove someone from an association
to ask for charity
(a derivative involving the base θάνατος[a] ‘death,’ 23.99) pertaining to having been condemned to death
senses.comment: The phrase ‘like men doomed to die’ may be rendered in some languages as ‘like men who will soon be killed’ or ‘… will soon be executed.’

senses.def: changing one’s belief, with focus upon that to which one turns
senses.comment: In analyzing the meaning of στρέφω[g], ἐπιστρέφω[b], and ἐπιστροφή[a] in such passages as Acts 15:3, it is difficult to determine the extent to which belief or behavior is primarily in focus. In the case of 1 Peter 2:25, one could certainly argue that the emphasis is upon the interpersonal relationship. It is therefore essential in rendering these terms not to narrow the meaning too much, for in this way one would certainly do violence to certain crucial semantic features.|For another interpretation of ἐπιστροφή in Acts 15:3, see 41.51.

senses.def: change in one’s manner of life in a particular direction, with the implication of turning back to God
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is not sufficient to simply translate ‘to change one’s manner of life,’ for this could either be neutral or even suggest a change for the worse. Therefore, it may be necessary in a number of instances to translate ‘to change one’s way of living as God would want’ or ‘to change and live like God would want one to live.’|For a different interpretation of ἐπιστροφή in Acts 15:3, see 31.60.

In a number of languages it may be necessary to use a term in Hebrews 11:29 which means ‘reddish,’ since an expression meaning ‘bright red’ might seem entirely inappropriate in speaking of a body of water.

senses.def: the mother of Timothy
a son of Jacob and ancestor of an Israelite tribe
the territory of the tribe of Zebulun
a granddaughter of Herod I and wife of Herod Antipas

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: the warmest period of the year and primarily the season for the growth of vegetation
senses.comment: In some areas of the Tropics, there are difficulties involved in arriving at a satisfactory term for θέρος. It may not be possible, for example, to use ‘the warm season,’ since that may refer to the end of a dry season just before the rains begin. Normally, therefore, one can equate θέρος with ‘the rainy season,’ but a context such as Luke 21:30 may be difficult, for one would not normally say ‘when you see that the trees are putting out leaves, you know that the rainy season is near,’ for trees normally do not put out the leaves until after the rainy season has begun. It may, therefore, be necessary to render Luke 21:30 as ‘when you see the trees putting out leaves, you know that the time for growth is near’ or ‘… the time for trees to produce fruit.’

senses.def: to cause someone to become well again after having been sick
senses.comment: In a number of languages there are different terms for ‘healing’ depending upon the type of sickness or illness which is involved.

senses.def: a soldier who fights on horseback

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: to be in a seated position
to remain for some time in a place, often with the implication of a settled situation
a province in the interior of Asia Minor

to reestablish proper friendly interpersonal relations after these have been disrupted or broken (the componential features of this series of meanings involve (1) disruption of friendly relations because of (2) presumed or real provocation (3) overt behavior designed to remove hostility, and (4) restoration of original friendly relations)
glosses: to make things right with one another
senses.comment: Because of the variety and complexity of the components involved in reconciliation, it is often necessary to use an entire phrase in order to communicate satisfactorily the meanings of the terms in this subdomain. In some languages, however, reconciliation is often spoken of in idiomatic terms, for example, ‘to cause to become friends again,’ ‘to cause to snap fingers again’ (a symbol of friendly interpersonal relations in many parts of Africa), ‘to cause to be one again,’ or ‘to take away the separation.’ A particularly crucial element in terms for reconciliation is the assigning of responsibility for original guilt in causing the estrangement. Some terms, for example, imply that the individual who initiates reconciliation is by doing so admitting his guilt in causing the estrangement. This, of course, provides a completely untenable meaning for reconciliation in speaking of God reconciling people to himself through Christ.|In a number of languages the contextual basis for an expression for reconciliation is often found in terms relating to the reconciliation of husbands and wives. Such expressions fit in well with many contexts in the Scriptures, especially in speaking of reconciliation of people to God, since God is frequently referred to as the husband and the believers as the wife.

senses.def: to cause something to become cool
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to render this expression in Luke 16:24 as ‘to cause my tongue to feel cool.’

senses.def: (derivative of κερδαίνω[a] ‘to earn, to gain,’ 57.189) that which is gained or earned
senses.comment: κέρδος in the sense of ‘gain’ is not restricted, however, to monetary gain or profit. It may refer to any kind of benefit or advantage, for example, ἐμοὶ γὰρ τὸ ζῆν Χριστὸς καὶ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν κέρδος ‘for me life is Christ, and death is a gain’ Philippians 1:21.

senses.def: the husband of Μαρία 5, one of the women at the crucifixion
a relatively small and often temporary type of object on which a person may lie or recline; made of reeds or cloth; thin and light for carrying
senses.comment: In a number of contexts the terms κλινίδιον, κλινάριον, and κράβαττος refer to cots or stretchers on which sick or convalescent persons might be resting or on which they could be transported. There is no NT context in which these terms refer to couches on which people reclined while eating.

senses.def: the imperial governor of Syria
a member of the tribe of Levi and having the responsibility to serve as an assistant to Jewish priests
senses.comment: In most languages Λευίτης has simply been transliterated, but in other languages it is rendered as ‘assistant priest,’ especially in those contexts in which religious activity is involved.

senses.def: to release or set free, with the implied analogy to the process of freeing a slave
senses.comment: In a number of languages one cannot speak of ‘being set free’ without specifying the particular manner or circumstances involved. In the case of Luke 24:21, for example, it may be necessary to translate ‘to liberate Israel’ as ‘to cause Israel to be free from foreign control’ or ‘… from the power of Rome.’ A similar type of translation may be required in Luke 2:38, but in the case of Ephesians 1:7 it may be necessary to specify ‘we are set free from sin’ or ‘we are set free from our bad desires.’

senses.def: to provide information about a person or an event concerning which the speaker has direct knowledge
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is necessary to indicate specifically what is the content of a witness, so that, for example, in Luke 21:13 it may be necessary to say ‘this is your chance to witness to the good news’ or ‘… to tell about the good news’ or ‘… to tell what you yourselves know about the good news.’

senses.def: (derivative of μαρτυρέω[a] ‘to witness,’ 33.262) the content of what is witnessed or said
senses.comment: In a number of languages one must specify the content of the witness, and it also may be necessary to indicate the agent who is engaged in the witnessing. For example, in Mark 14:55 it may be necessary to translate ‘they tried to find someone who would testify against Jesus’ or ‘… say something against Jesus.’ In 1 Corinthians 1:6 it may be necessary to translate ‘what we told you from personal experience about Christ has become so firmly fixed in you’ or ‘… has become so much a part of you.’

senses.def: to bring about a mutually accepted agreement between two or more parties, with the probable additional component of making something certain
senses.comment: Since one who was a μεσίτης (31.22) often acted as one who provided the surety or guarantee of an agreement or arrangement, there is a significant component of certainty involved in μεσιτεύω. Hence, one may understand this as implying not only the agreement but the guarantee of its validity.

senses.def: a marker of coordinate negativized expressions (combination of the negative particle μή[a] ‘not,’ 69.3, and the postpositive conjunction τέ[a] ‘and,’ 89.95)
(figurative extension of meaning of μυκτηρίζω ‘to turn up the nose at,’ not occurring in the NT) to ridicule in a sneering and contemptuous way

senses.subdomain: Land in Contrast With the Sea
senses.def: an area of land completely surrounded by water
senses.comment: In some languages an island can only be designated by a description, for example, ‘a small country in the sea’ or ‘some land surrounded by water.’

senses.def: pertaining to being dry
(a figurative extension of meaning of ξηρός[a] ‘dry, withered,’ 79.80) pertaining to a shrunken, withered, and hence immobile part of the body

senses.subdomain: Land in Contrast With the Sea
senses.def: dry land, in contrast with the sea
senses.comment: In a number of languages a clear distinction is made between terms which designate land in contrast with water and those which designate cultivated land. Even in English the normal term for land close to water is ‘shore’ or ‘coast,’ and therefore one may translate Matthew 14:24 as ‘the boat was already far away from the shore.’ Similarly, in Acts 27:27 one may translate ‘we were getting close to shore.’

senses.def: to cause the complete destruction or ruin of someone or something
to see
senses.comment: As in a number of other contexts, ἀδελφοῖς in 1 Corinthians 15:6 may be rendered as ‘fellow believers’ or simply ‘believers.’

senses.subdomain: To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
senses.def: to take special notice of something, with the implication of concerning oneself
senses.comment: Though the terms ἐπιβλέπω, ἐπεῖδον (ἐφοράω), and ὁράω suggest as a result of their central meanings some measure of visual perception, what is involved in these specific contexts is much more than visual perception. The focus is actually upon intellectual activity and concern.

senses.def: to come to understand as the result of perception
to go to see a person on the basis of friendship and with helpful intent
(a figurative extension of meaning of ὁράω[a] ‘to see,’ 24.1) to experience an event or state, normally in negative expressions indicating what one will not experience
to acquire information, with focus upon the event of perception
to take responsibility for causing something to happen
glosses: to see to it that something happens
to arrange for something to happen

senses.def: prompter of attention, which serves also to emphasize the following statement
prompter of attention, which serves also to emphasize the following statement
a marker of strong emphasis, indicating complete validation of what is said
a man whose wife is referred to in the genealogy of Jesus
a title for God, literally: all powerful
glosses: the One who has all power
senses.comment: In some languages the Almighty as a title for God may be expressed as ‘the one who controls everything’ or ‘the one who commands all things and all people.’

senses.def: to watch closely or diligently
pertaining to being in control

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
senses.def: a small writing tablet (normally made of wood)
a marker of an agent relation with a numerable event
to do or perform (highly generic for almost any type of activity)
to cause a state to be
to engage in an activity involving considerable expenditure of effort
to produce something new, with the implication of using materials already in existence (in contrast with κτίζω ‘to create,’ 42.35)
to behave or act in a particular way with respect to someone

senses.subdomain: Assign to a Role or Function
senses.def: to cause someone to assume a particular type of function
glosses: to cause people to assume responsibilities for a task

senses.def: to gain by means of one’s activity or investment
senses.comment: In many languages, it may be quite impossible to speak of ‘one mina has earned five minas’ or even ‘one coin has earned five coins’ (Luke 19:18). It may be necessary to turn this into an expression involving a human agent, for example, ‘I have earned five minas with the one that you gave me.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally to make fruit) to produce fruit or seed (of plants)
(an idiom, literally to make fruit) to cause results to exist

senses.subdomain: Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to do what is enough) to cause someone to be pleased by doing what will satisfy
glosses: to act in a pleasing manner

senses.def: an indefinite position in space
a degree which falls just short of some point on a scale of extent
senses.comment: In some languages this expression in Romans 4:19 may be accurately represented by a translation meaning literally ‘he lacked only a little of being a hundred years old.’

senses.def: to announce openly what is to happen in the future
to cause something to roll up to or against
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to distinguish in verbs for ‘roll’ whether the object in question is ball-shaped or disc-shaped. The stone at the tomb is more likely to have been disc-shaped.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of πταίω ‘to stumble,’ not occurring in the NT) to fail to keep the law (of God)
the wife of Jacob
an island off the west coast of Asia Minor
the name for a system of water supply in Jerusalem; the pool of Siloam was probably the basin into which the water flowed
the son and successor of David

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the trunk of the body from the neck to the abdomen
disorderly mob revolt, with special implications of uproar and disturbance
senses.comment: In a number of languages the meaning of ‘riot’ may be best expressed as ‘people shouting strongly against’ or ‘people shouting and fighting against’ or ‘a mob shouting against the government.’

senses.def: a marker of an associative relation, often involving joint participation in some activity
a marker of linkage between objects or between events, but without specifying the precise positional or functional relation

senses.subdomain: Agent, Personal or Nonpersonal, Causative or Immediate, Direct or Indirect
senses.def: (followed by the genitive; an idiom, literally: with the hand of) a marker of an associated agent
to be at a place which is next to something else
senses.comment: In a number of languages the concept of ‘being next to’ may be best expressed as ‘there was no space between.’

senses.subdomain: Cause To Be Safe, Free from Danger
senses.def: to rescue from danger and to restore to a former state of safety and well being
a state of having been saved
the process of being saved
senses.comment: Although it is difficult and sometimes impossible to determine whether σωτηρία refers to the state of being saved (21.25) or the process of being saved, in some languages it is obligatory to choose one or the other meaning.

senses.def: a person who sends greetings in Romans 16:22
to hurt or wound, normally resulting in some mark or permanent scar on the body

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to be insolently mistreated
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ὕβρις in 2 Corinthians 12:10 as actual physical violence (see 20.19) or as insults (see 33.391).

senses.def: the condition resulting from violence or mistreatment
senses.comment: It is possible to interpret ὕβρις in 2 Corinthians 12:10 as ‘insults’ (see 33.391) or as ‘insolent mistreatment’ (see 88.131).

senses.def: (derivative of ὑβρίζω[b] ‘to insult,’ 33.390) the content of an insulting statement
senses.comment: In 2 Corinthians 12:10 it is not possible to determine whether ὕβρις refers to the content of the slanderous words or to the event of being slandered. For other interpretations of ὕβρις in 2 Corinthians 12:10, see 88.131 and 20.19.

senses.subdomain: Pattern, Model, Example, and Corresponding Representation
senses.def: a model of behavior as an example to be imitated or to be avoided
to become visible, implying an extraordinary and startling appearance

senses.subdomain: Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
senses.def: to earnestly aspire to something, implying strong ambition for some goal
glosses: to make something one’s ambition to
senses.comment: An equivalent of φιλοτιμεῖσθαι ἡσυχάζειν in 1 Thessalonians 4:11 may be in some languages ‘do everything you can to live the quiet life.’

senses.def: any type of sound, including human speech, but normally a distinctive type of sound as opposed to confused noise
senses.comment: In many languages an important distinction is made between verbal sounds, that is to say, the sounds of speech, and non-verbal sounds. In some languages musical sounds also require a very special type of terminology, often with distinctions made depending upon the type of instrument involved.

senses.def: the human voice as an instrument of communication
senses.comment: In a number of languages one cannot speak of a voice without identifying who is speaking, and since the context indicates clearly that this is God, one can only say ‘God’s voice came from the cloud’ or ‘God spoke from a cloud.’

senses.def: the sound of a cry or shout
a verbal code, whether oral or written, as a basic means of communication
senses.comment: It is possible to interpret φωνή in 2 Peter 2:16 as ‘voice’ (see 33.103).

senses.def: a city in Galilee
providing harmful information about a person, often spoken in whispers or in low voice, with the implication that such information is not widely known and therefore should presumably be kept secret
